objects.name: SSP Brick (Alpaca4d)
objects.desc:
Construct a SSP (Stabilized Single Point) Brick element from an eight vertex mesh.
The mesh is reordered into the node order OpenSees wants and checked for a positive Jacobian at every corner - a brick wound the wrong way round, or twisted, is one the solver accepts and answers with the wrong sign rather than rejecting.

A solid has no local axes. OpenSees gives neither element an orientation argument, and an nD material has no orientation either, so the material's own directions - Ex, Ey and Ez on an Elastic Orthotropic - are the global X, Y and Z, and so are the stresses read back. To align an orthotropic material with the part, rotate the model.
Where a solid meets a beam or a shell at a point, the two are tied in translation only: a solid node carries no moment, so the junction is a pin.

objects.name: Support (Alpaca4d)
objects.desc:
A support. Rigid: fixes the node along and about the axes of the Position's plane you choose. Elastic: a spring along or about each axis of the plane. Compression Only: holds the node only while it pushes into the support, along the plane's Z, and lets it lift - after a gap, if there is one.
Elastic and Compression Only never fix the node themselves, so a Rigid support on the same point can hold what they leave free: a pinned bearing that can lift is a Compression Only support with a Rigid one holding Tx and Ty only.
Reaction Force gives a spring support a row of its own, with the spring's force.

objects.name: BESO Topology (Alpaca4d)
objects.desc:
Finds where a solid needs its material by BESO, bi-directional evolutionary structural optimisation. It starts from every solid of the model and takes EvolutionRate of the volume away each iteration, until VolumeFraction is left: each iteration keeps the elements that work hardest - their strain energy per volume, smoothed over FilterRadius and averaged with the iteration before - and lets the rest go, or brings void ones back. Every element is solid or void all along, so every iteration is a design of its own, of the volume reached: drag Step to look through them.
A void element keeps a billionth of its stiffness instead of being cut out, so the mesh stays as it is. Bricks are solved as OpenSees' eight point brick (stdBrick), and every solid needs an Elastic Isotropic Material, as in Topology Optimisation. The run stops once the volume is reached and the compliance has settled: the last five iterations' within Tolerance of the five before.
Set Run to true to start. Switching Run off pauses it; on again, it goes on from where it stopped. Changing any input but Iterations and Tolerance starts it again from the beginning.

objects.name: Analysis Settings (Alpaca4d)
objects.desc:
Collects everything OpenSees needs in order to solve - constraint handler, numberer, system of equations, convergence test, solution algorithm, integrator and stepping - into the one object Run Analysis takes.
Every input has a default, so an unconnected component already describes a valid linear static analysis. For a dynamic one set AnalysisType to Transient, and give it a Newmark or Central Difference Integrator, an Analysis Step with Dt, and a Damping.

objects.name: Run Analysis (Alpaca4d)
objects.desc:
Writes the assembled model out as an OpenSees script, solves it, and returns the model with its results attached.
Results are recorded to a recorder.mpco file beside the Grasshopper document and read back by the 08_NumericalOutput components; an MPCO Recorder connected to Assemble Model chooses what the file holds, and what it is called. When a run fails the AlpacaModel output comes out empty - read the log output to find out why.

objects.name: View Results_WIP (Alpaca4d)
objects.desc:
Draw any result on the model: displacements, beam force diagrams, beam stresses, shell forces, shell stresses, solid stresses, reactions.
Pick the result, the component and the unit from the dropdowns. ElementId shows only some of the elements and greys the rest, so what you are looking at stays in the model around it.
With Extruded beams on, beam stresses that differ across a section - σx, σMy, σMz, τV, τT, Von Mises - are painted point by point over it; drawn as lines, each section shows its worst.
A vibration or buckling mode is drawn at deformation scale 1 with its largest movement as far off the model as the diagrams stand; any other displacement at true size. On a natural vibration or buckling model the scale runs from -2 to 2, so Animate swings the mode both ways.
Work in progress, and meant to grow into the replacement for the separate view components.

objects.name: Panel
objects.desc: A panel for custom notes and text values
objects.text:
Bridge carved out of its block - a BESO Topology example.

The block of the Topology Optimisation example: steel, 16 m long, 2 m wide and 4 m high, pinned along both ends of its bottom, its top layer a deck kept solid under 10 kN/m2. BESO Topology starts from the whole block and takes 2% of what is left away each iteration - the bricks that work least go, and some come back - until a fifth of the block below the deck is left. Every brick is solid or void all along.

1. Set Run to true. The run goes on its own thread: the Surface preview and the outputs follow it.
2. Volume comes down from 1 to VolumeFraction in about 80 iterations; then the design settles, and the run stops once the compliance has.
3. Drag Step back to go through the designs: each one is a bridge of the volume reached, from the whole block down - choose the one you want.
4. Once the run has stopped, enable Run Analysis and Legend: AlpacaModel is the design shown as a model, and View Results colours it by Von Mises stress.

Each SSP Brick is solved as OpenSees' eight point brick, and a void brick keeps a billionth of its stiffness. Above 500 bricks BESO Topology needs a license.
